newsitem.title: UK: Lockheed, Alenia in airlifter venture.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed, Alenia in airlifter venture.

text.p: U.S. defence and aerospace giant Lockheed Martin Corp announced on Tuesday a major joint venture agreement with Italy's Alenia Aerospazio, a a unit of state-owned Finmeccanica, to develop and market a new tactical airlifter.
The agreement was unveiled at the aerospace industry showcase Farnborough International. Lockheed and Alenia will be equal partners in the new joint venture.
Lockheed said the airlifter will be based on Alenia's G 222 model and related systems developed for the U.S. group's C-13OJ Hercules.

The agreement to develop the new airlifter, dubbed C-27"J', will see Lockheed take charge of engineering, manage product support and develop a worldwide marketing organisation for the model. Alenia will also provide engineering capability as well as assembly and flight testing in Italy.
John McLellan, president of Lockheed Martin Aeronautical Systems, said: "There is a tremendous market for a technically advanced medium tactical airlifter".

"This agreement not only is the beginning of what we are confident will be a successfull partnership, but also sits comfortably with Lockheed Martin's strategy to widen its presence in the global airlift market," he added.
